tasks.short: Calculate takeoff speed from aircraft and operating conditions.

steps.what: Confirm aircraft configuration, mass, altitude, temperature, runway and wind inputs
Calculate the speed needed to become airborne using aircraft-specific performance software
Check calculated speeds, operating limits and consistency with the actual conditions
Prepare and check the final takeoff performance record for this flight
Save the approved performance record in the electronic flight bag

tasks.design: Configure an existing aircraft-specific performance application in {OTHER}, the operator's approved electronic flight bag. The pilot confirms all inputs, reviews calculated speeds and checks the complete record before a separate save. No new performance algorithm, model interpretation or aircraft control is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manual chart calculations are mechanical, but wrong inputs or aircraft data produce an unsafe result.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing performance software can calculate from aircraft-specific data and explicit operating inputs.
tasks.still_hard: Input validity, limits and changed conditions remain the pilot's responsibility.
tasks.human_edge: Reject a plausible speed that does not match the actual aircraft or runway situation.
tasks.altitude: Less manual calculation with all operational checks retained.

evidence.claim: The digest describes Lido Flight 4D takeoff and landing performance capability; suitability for this aircraft is not established.

assumptions: Shares are provisional for a pilot currently performing manual chart calculations. Existing EFB calculations/runtime earn no new saving; no reduced vigilance or flight time is claimed.

Pilot captures aircraft_type, registration, configuration, takeoff_mass, pressure_altitude, temperature, runway_condition, runway_length, wind_direction and wind_speed in s1. Loading staff/actual weighing supply mass inputs, weather service supplies timestamped observations, operator supplies current manual/database. Capture and source checking stay full time.

Only an operator-accepted application with current aircraft data is considered. Missing, stale, mismatched or out-of-envelope input returns to the operator's manual procedure. Test against independent manual cases across the relevant envelope before adoption.

s4 checks flight_id, calculation_version and actual inputs. a1 binds that completed record after its final check; changed loading/weather requires recalculation and a new check, not reuse of the old approval. No automatic takeoff-setting write or external send occurs.
research_questions: Does an existing accepted application cover the actual aircraft and conditions and remove manual calculation work?

tasks.short: Monitor engines, fuel consumption and aircraft systems during flight.

steps.what: Monitor engine operation, fuel consumption and aircraft-system indications throughout flight
Interpret trends, cross-check fuel usage and respond through the applicable aircraft procedures
Prepare and check the monitoring record using verified aircraft-recorded factual fields
Commit the approved monitoring record to the operator's flight record system

tasks.design: Keep continuous monitoring and all trend interpretation human using {OTHER}, the existing aircraft instruments. Where the operator already has an authorised aircraft monitoring export, configure factual field reuse in its flight-record system after the operational phase. The pilot writes operational observations, checks the complete record and approves a separate commit. No display, warning or aircraft control changes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Monitoring is continuous situational awareness; occasional numeric record entry is only a small separate component.
tasks.enabler_now: An existing approved export may reuse timestamped numeric fields in the operator record.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising abnormal combinations and deciding how to respond remain piloting work.
tasks.human_edge: Integrate aircraft indications with what is actually happening in flight.
tasks.altitude: Small factual record-entry gain; no monitoring duty is reduced.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: existing authorised aircraft exports may support flight-record field reuse; availability for this aircraft is unverified.

assumptions: Shares are provisional for monitoring plus its existing operator record. No saving is attributed to looking away from instruments, replacing an emergency procedure or reducing flight time.

Aircraft monitoring equipment produces registration, timestamp, engine_parameter, unit and fuel_quantity in an already authorised export. No new sensor installation or live interface is assumed. s3 pilot verifies flight match and enters observations, exceptions and any missing values within retained 5.6 hours; no inferred data fills gaps.

Only actual repeated numeric entry is shortened; if no export or record exists, do not adopt this change or invent one. Existing native import earns no new saving. s3's final check and a1 bind the completed record and flight before s4; edits revoke approval.

No automatic defect report or maintenance message is introduced. A genuine defect requires the actual operator reporting procedure with its own approved report and send, without any claimed saving here.
research_questions: Is there an existing approved export and an actual repeated entry action that can be removed after flight?

tasks.short: Order safety-related changes to fuel, loads, routes or schedules.

steps.what: Assess the safety constraint and verify current fuel, loading and departure conditions
Compare feasible fuel or loading alternatives in aircraft-specific flight planning software
Decide the fuel or loading change needed to ensure flight safety
Prepare the exact fuel change order and aircraft identification
Approve the complete fuel order, units, target aircraft and supplier recipient
Send the approved fuel change order to the handling supplier
Verify delivered fuel and resulting loading before accepting the changed conditions
outputs: pilot-verified actual changed fuel and loading

steps.what: Write and approve the final flight-change record using verified actual quantities
inputs: pilot-verified actual changed fuel and loading

steps.what: Commit the approved actual flight-change record

tasks.design: For a predeparture fuel-change case, use existing aircraft-specific planning in {OTHER}, the EFB/flight-planning system, to compare alternatives. Keep the safety decision and actual delivery check human. Configure the existing handling-message channel to send only the completed approved order, then separately save the checked actual flight-change record. A transmitted order never counts as delivered fuel.
tasks.previous_blocker: Ordering a change and knowing the aircraft's actual changed state are different events.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing planning calculations and handling-message routing can assist the pilot without deciding safety.
tasks.still_hard: Operational trade-offs, unit errors and verifying actual fuel/loading require the pilot.
tasks.human_edge: Reject an apparently adequate plan when actual conditions or confirmed delivery differ.
tasks.altitude: Less mechanical option calculation and approved order transfer; unchanged safety decisions.

evidence.claim: The digest describes Lido Flight 4D fuel/profile planning capability; local aircraft and message-channel suitability remain unverified.

assumptions: Provisional shares describe the fuel branch of a task covering fuel, load, route or schedule changes. This is not an automatic inflight-diversion workflow. Existing calculations and message routing receive no additional credit.

s1 pilot captures registration, flight_id, actual_fuel, fuel_unit, confirmed_mass, departure_conditions and required_reserve under the operator's actual procedure. Existing aircraft/load records and weather service supply the raw facts; interpretation and missing data stay full time.

s4 pilot supplies requested_quantity, fuel_type, unit, aircraft_location and supplier_contact. s5 checks the actual complete order; a1 binds those fields and recipient. A changed quantity or target revokes approval; no model chooses or sends an order.

Supplier produces delivery_confirmation, delivered_quantity and unit; s7 pilot checks these against the physical indication and revised loading. Capture/check effort stays full time. Mismatch returns to human resolution before acceptance.

s8 records actual_quantity, final_mass, reason and source confirmations; a2 binds that completed final record after actual verification. No prior order approval substitutes for actual-record approval. Other required revised performance/flight-plan actions follow the operator's procedures without claimed saving here.
research_questions: Can the existing tools reduce real calculation and order transfer while preserving verification of actual delivered fuel?

tasks.short: Contact control towers by radio for clearances and instructions.

steps.what: Select and check the correct control-tower radio frequency and aircraft identification
Formulate and check the final radio request before transmitting
Contact the control tower by transmitting the checked radio request
Listen to and interpret the tower clearance or arrival instructions
Write the received clearance on the pilot's existing clearance scratchpad
Check the full intended readback against the received clearance and aircraft context
Transmit the checked readback or request clarification over the aircraft radio

tasks.design: Retain the actual {OTHER} aircraft-radio workflow. Split request preparation from transmission, and split clearance receipt, scratchpad writing, checked readback and readback transmission. Existing native radio functions and a standard clearance-note format are considered; neither removes the pilot's need to listen, check and communicate the exact current instruction.
tasks.previous_blocker: Radio traffic is time-dependent and an instruction must be matched to the correct aircraft and situation.
tasks.enabler_now: No additional mechanism is established beyond existing aircraft radio and clearance-note tools.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous calls, changed clearances and conflicting situational information require immediate pilot judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise an unexpected or unclear instruction and seek clarification.
tasks.altitude: No demonstrated saving after separating the note and both transmissions.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: pilot radio clearance exchanges require context-specific listening and readback; a scratchpad can already use a standard concise format.

assumptions: Shares are provisional for pilot labour only; tower response time is not claimed as displaced. The diagram describes a normal exchange, with any clarification repeating the relevant checked request and send at full time.

s1 pilot obtains frequency and callsign from current aeronautical information and actual flight context. s5 pilot explicitly captures clearance_limit, route, altitude, frequency and transponder fields only when provided; hearing/writing stays fully counted. Missing or unclear fields require clarification, not a transcript guess.

a1 is the pilot's ordinary check of the final intended utterance immediately before push-to-talk; a2 is the corresponding check of the actual final readback. These are not added remote approvals. Any changed utterance is checked again before transmission.

Native frequency selection and a clearance-note template were considered. No duplicated later report, database commit or extra notification is assumed; the scratchpad is already the direct working record. A speech tool adds verification without an established saving, so no new system is proposed.
research_questions: Is there any real duplicated clearance-note action beyond the direct working scratchpad represented here?

incremental.description: No new software; retain the existing aircraft-radio and scratchpad workflow

approvals.approved_version: s2 final pilot-checked radio request for the current aircraft and frequency
s6 final checked readback or clarification utterance

role.altitude: Retain aircraft command and situational awareness while reducing only verified mechanical planning and record work.
reach: Help operations teams distinguish approved plans, transmitted orders and verified actual aircraft state.
role.ambitious_version: A commercial pilot supported by accepted calculation and record tools, with operational decisions and communications remaining under pilot control.
